nodes.summary: The Apollonian packing generated by a Descartes configuration $C_0$ is the set of circles occurring in some configuration reachable from $C_0$ by Apollonian swaps. When $C_0$ contains a circle enclosing the other three, every circle reachable this way lies inside it and the packing is bounded.
nodes.title: Apollonian circle packing

nodes.summary: For a bounded packing $P$, $N_P(T)$ is the number of circles of $P$ whose curvature is at most $T$. The bounding circle is counted with its unsigned curvature $1/r$ rather than its signed curvature $-1/r$; this changes $N_P(T)$ by at most one and does not affect asymptotics.
nodes.title: Circle-counting function

nodes.summary: Let $c_1, \dots, c_4 \in \mathbb{C}$ and nonzero real numbers $s_1, \dots, s_4$ satisfy $|c_i - c_j|^2 = (s_i + s_j)^2$ for $i \ne j$, and let $k_i = 1/s_i$. Then The $s_i$ are signed radii: positive for a circle whose interior is disjoint from the others, negative for a circle enclosing the others, so that tangent circles have centers at distance $|s_i + s_j|$.
nodes.title: Complex Descartes theorem for signed radii

nodes.summary: Let four circles in the plane $\mathbb{C}$ have centers $c_i$, radii $r_i > 0$ and signed curvatures $k_i$, in either configuration of Descartes' circle theorem: (a) pairwise externally tangent, $|c_i - c_j| = r_i + r_j$, with $k_i = 1/r_i$; or (b) one circle $e$ internally tangent to the three others, $|c_e - c_j| = r_e - r_j$, which are pairwise externally tangent, with $k_e = -1/r_e$ and $k_j = 1/r_j$ for…
nodes.title: Complex Descartes theorem

nodes.summary: The reciprocal `1 / radius` of its radius (H. Oh, arXiv:1312.1383v2, Section 1).
nodes.title: Curvature of a plane circle

nodes.summary: Let $s_1, s_2$ be spheres of positive radii in a Euclidean affine space that are externally tangent at $p$ in the sense of Mathlib's `Sphere.IsExtTangentAt` ($p$ lies on both spheres and on the segment joining their centers). Then $s_1 \cap s_2 = \{p\}$. Mathlib characterises external tangency by the distance of the centers (`Sphere.isExtTangent_iff_dist_center`) but does not state this uniqueness: any common point…

nodes.summary: Let $s_1$ be a sphere of positive radius $r_1$ internally tangent at $p$ to a sphere $s_2$ of larger radius $r_2$, in the sense of Mathlib's `Sphere.IsIntTangentAt` ($p$ lies on both spheres and the center of $s_1$ lies between the center of $s_2$ and $p$). Then $s_1 \cap s_2 = \{p\}$. The radii must differ: two equal spheres are internally tangent at each of their points. This strengthens Mathlib's…
nodes.title: Internally tangent spheres meet at exactly one point

nodes.summary: A Descartes configuration is a quadruple of four distinct, pairwise tangent circles such that the three points at which any one circle touches the other three are distinct, that is, no three of the circles have a common tangent at a common point. Tangency is a one-point intersection. A configuration of concentric circles or a pencil of circles tangent at one point is excluded. The tests check that the circles of…
nodes.title: Descartes configuration

nodes.summary: If the centers $c_1, c_2$ of two spheres of positive radii $r_1, r_2$ are at distance $r_1 + r_2$, then the spheres are externally tangent, in the sense of Mathlib's `Sphere.IsExtTangentAt`, at the point $c_1 + \frac{r_1}{r_1 + r_2}(c_2 - c_1)$ of the segment of centers. This is the witness used in the proof of Mathlib's `Sphere.isExtTangent_iff_dist_center`, stated here explicitly so that the tangency point can be…
nodes.title: The external tangency point of two spheres

nodes.summary: If a sphere of radius $r_1 > 0$ has its center $c_1$ at distance $r_2 - r_1$ from the center $c_2$ of a sphere of larger radius $r_2$, then it is internally tangent to that sphere, in the sense of Mathlib's `Sphere.IsIntTangentAt`, at the point $c_2 + \frac{r_2}{r_2 - r_1}(c_1 - c_2)$. This is the witness used in the proof of Mathlib's `Sphere.isIntTangent_iff_dist_center`, stated explicitly.
nodes.title: The internal tangency point of two spheres

nodes.summary: The configurations reachable from $C_0$ are generated by swaps: in a reachable configuration $C$, replace the circle $C_i$ by a different circle $D$ such that $D$ and the three circles $C_j$, $j \ne i$, again form a Descartes configuration. By the theorem of Apollonius there are exactly two circles tangent to three mutually tangent circles with distinct tangency points, so $D$ is the other one; in a bounded packing…
nodes.title: Configurations reachable by Apollonian swaps

nodes.title: Kontorovich–Oh circle-counting theorem

nodes.summary: Each of the four circles of the initial Descartes configuration $C_0$ belongs to the Apollonian packing that $C_0$ generates (it occurs in the configuration $C_0$ itself, reached by no swap).
nodes.title: The initial circles belong to the packing

nodes.summary: A plane circle is a sphere of Mathlib's `EuclideanGeometry.Sphere ℂ` (a center in $\mathbb{C}$ and a real radius) whose radius is positive. Lines, the circles of curvature zero, are not included, so the packing definitions of this topic describe bounded packings. Being a Mathlib sphere, a plane circle can use Mathlib's tangency API (`Sphere.IsExtTangentAt`, `Sphere.IsIntTangentAt`) directly.
nodes.title: Circle in the plane

nodes.summary: The residual set $\operatorname{Res}(P)$ of a packing $P$ is the closure in $\mathbb{C}$ of the union of its circles. For an Apollonian packing it is the limit set of the Apollonian group, a fractal of Hausdorff dimension $\alpha \approx 1.30568$, strictly between $1$ and $2$; $\alpha$ does not depend on the packing, since any two Apollonian packings are related by a Möbius transformation.
nodes.title: Residual set of an Apollonian packing

nodes.summary: If two circles meet exactly at $p$, then so do the same two circles taken in the other order: the definition is symmetric because set intersection is commutative.
nodes.title: Tangency is symmetric

nodes.summary: If the centers of two plane circles of radii $r_1, r_2$ are at distance $r_1 + r_2$, the circles meet exactly at the point $c_1 + \frac{r_1}{r_1 + r_2}(c_2 - c_1)$ of the segment of centers. It combines the explicit external tangency point with the uniqueness of the common point.
nodes.title: Externally tangent circles touch at one point

nodes.summary: If the second of two plane circles has the smaller radius and their centers are at distance $r_1 - r_2$, the circles meet exactly at the point $c_1 + \frac{r_1}{r_1 - r_2}(c_2 - c_1)$ of the ray from the first center through the second. It combines the explicit internal tangency point with the uniqueness of the common point.
nodes.title: Internally tangent circles touch at one point

nodes.summary: Two plane circles that are externally tangent at $p$ in the sense of Mathlib's `Sphere.IsExtTangentAt` are tangent at $p$ in the sense used for Descartes configurations: $p$ is their only common point.
nodes.title: Mathlib's external tangency gives tangency

nodes.summary: If a plane circle $D$ is internally tangent at $p$ to a plane circle $C$ of larger radius, in the sense of Mathlib's `Sphere.IsIntTangentAt`, then $C$ and $D$ are tangent at $p$: $p$ is their only common point.
nodes.title: Mathlib's internal tangency gives tangency

nodes.summary: Two circles are tangent at `p` when `p` is their only common point.
nodes.title: Tangency of two circles at a point

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
